name: vehicle-driver-assignment-visual
description: Visual check: assign qualified driver to vehicle, verify driver info, enforce one driver per vehicle

steps.description: cash:75000 (dusty_hollow's own $50,000 + one extra debris_hauler's $25,000) funds the second vehicle bought below (issue #585) -- it is spent in full at that step, so every cash figure from there through the rest of the file is unchanged from before this override.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.

expect.note: unchanged from before — driving.truck was already the driver role's Rookie starting qualification at level 1; this command reproduces the same level, not a change

steps.description: Opens the Vehicles panel via a real UI click so the after-qualified/after-unqualified shots capture the .bs-vehicle-driver-name indicator instead of a 3D orbit — the panel stays open for every later step once opened here (#411).

expect.note: arrival-gated like surveys — the driver walks to the vehicle before boarding, `vehicle list` still shows driver:none right after this click

steps.description: Second vehicle, bought so employee #2 can be assigned a driver seat that isn't already taken (issue #585) -- vehicle #1 already has employee #1 as its driver, and canAssignDriver (VehicleDriverAssignment.ts) checks the target vehicle's own driver slot, not employee #1's assignment, so this needs its own free vehicle rather than a second attempt on #1.

Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- grants employee #2 (a blaster) the driving.truck licence needed to crew the second vehicle below; the player-facing path is `employee train` (issue #585, mirrors the assign_skill step above for employee #1).

expect.note: employee #1's driving.truck(1) + employee #2's own starting blasting(1) + this grant's driving.truck(1) = 3

steps.description: Retargeted to vehicle #2 (issue #585): the original `vehicle driver 1 2` failed no matter what, because canAssignDriver checks the requested employee's licence before it ever checks whether the target vehicle already has a driver -- vehicle #1 keeps the assignment proven above untouched, and employee #2, now licenced, genuinely takes vehicle #2's open seat. Real click (mirrors step 5's `vehicle driver 1 1`), not a bootstrap command -- the panel opened at step 4 stays open (#411), so vehicle #2's own assign button is already reachable.
